scope: Labelled browser wallet/API fixtures; actual local Groth16 proof; deterministic tax outline; separately recorded public native NEAR CLI testnet evidence. No live browser-wallet USDC, AI-provider or professional approval claim.

chapters.title: Private settlement. Shared confidence.
chapters.narration: Meet Core: private business settlement on NEAR, with evidence you choose to share. Built for business invoices, worker payments, and contractor payouts.

chapters.title: Distributed principal. Shared proof.
chapters.scope: PROTOCOL ARCHITECTURE · PUBLIC METADATA REMAINS VISIBLE
chapters.narration: Principal stays in independent vaults. A shared zero knowledge note authorizes a funded vault to pay, without naming the input note. A global nullifier prevents a second spend.

chapters.title: Start with a signed invoice
chapters.scope: CONTROLLED BROWSER DEMO · FIXTURE WALLET AND API
chapters.narration: The recipient creates a signed invoice. Checkout verifies the request, payment unit, merchant, and trusted group before a payer selects an encrypted note.

chapters.title: Generate the proof locally
chapters.scope: REAL LOCAL GROTH16 PROOF · FIXTURE CHAIN CONTEXT
chapters.narration: Here, the browser generates a real Groth sixteen proof using verified proving files. Note secrets and the note password stay local. Proof generation can also be cancelled.

chapters.title: Review before every signature
chapters.scope: CONTROLLED BROWSER DEMO · NO PUBLIC USDC TRANSFER
chapters.narration: Review the amount and the added fifteen basis point fee. The recipient receives the full principal. Storage and network gas are separate, and each required wallet call is reviewed individually.

chapters.title: Confirm from finalized observations
chapters.scope: FIXTURE FINALITY OBSERVATION · NOT A LIVE WALLET RECEIPT
chapters.narration: The payment view reconciles finalized observations. An uncertain response stays unresolved until checked, avoiding an automatic second payment. This browser walkthrough uses a test wallet and API fixtures.

chapters.title: Turn evidence into a cited draft
chapters.scope: SOURCE-BOUND OUTLINE DEMO · NO LIVE AI OR PROFESSIONAL APPROVAL
chapters.narration: Teams can prepare cited tax and procedure drafts from verified rule calculations and selected evidence. This example uses deterministic outline mode. Unsupported obligations remain visible for review.

chapters.title: Separate preparation from approval
chapters.narration: Submit an immutable revision for another authorized reviewer. The author cannot approve their own preparation. Changes require a new revision, and source or permission changes invalidate reliance.

chapters.title: Fourteen real testnet transactions
chapters.scope: RECORDED PUBLIC TESTNET EVIDENCE · NATIVE NEAR · CLI WALLET
chapters.narration: Separately, the native NEAR software wallet run recorded fourteen real public testnet transactions. Two deposits of point one NEAR reached keyless vaults, followed by successful payouts.

chapters.title: A real failure. The original destination.
chapters.scope: RECORDED PUBLIC TESTNET EVIDENCE · RETRYABLE TO COMPLETE
chapters.narration: A missing recipient caused an actual failed transfer. After activating that same recipient, recovery kept the original nullifier, vault, amount, and destination. The retry charged no second protocol fee.

chapters.title: A prototype with explicit boundaries
chapters.scope: PRIVACY DEPENDS ON PARTICIPATION AND METADATA
chapters.narration: The read only verifier rechecks receipts, signatures, code, keys, and historical balances. This does not establish effective anonymity. Browser wallet and USDC public testnet qualification, live hosting, and production review remain separate.

chapters.title: Inspect. Run. Verify.
chapters.narration: Explore the three repositories, follow the quick start, and verify the published transaction evidence. Core: private settlement, shared confidence.
